objective: Test six independent return and protection mechanisms while adding explicit large-breakout precision and recall diagnostics.

candidates.concept: Risk assets should clear both an absolute trend test and the best defensive asset momentum hurdle.
candidates.fixed_rules: Monthly composite 63/126/252-session momentum; equal-weight up to three positively trending risk assets only when each beats the strongest defensive score, otherwise hold the strongest defensive asset.

candidates.concept: Continuous risk scaling may preserve more upside than binary exits while controlling volatility.
candidates.fixed_rules: Hold SPY only above its 200-session mean, scaled to a 12 percent annual volatility target using 60 sessions, with residual in SHY.

candidates.concept: Persistent defensive trends may provide positive participation during negative equity trends.
candidates.fixed_rules: Below the SPY 200-session mean, select the strongest asset among BIL, IEF, and GLD only when both 63- and 126-session returns are positive; otherwise SHY. Hold SPY when its trend is positive.

candidates.concept: A market near a medium-term high while sector breadth falls materially may be vulnerable.
candidates.fixed_rules: Rotate SPY to SHY when SPY is within two percent of its 63-session high and 50-session sector breadth has fallen at least 25 percentage points over 20 sessions.

candidates.concept: A breakout may be more reliable when the sector is also outperforming SPY.
candidates.fixed_rules: Hold the sector making a new 55-session closing high with a positive 200-session trend and at least three percentage points of 63-session relative strength versus SPY; otherwise SHY.

candidates.concept: Waiting for multi-session confirmation after a sharp decline may avoid premature first-reversal entries.
candidates.fixed_rules: After an eight-percent 10-session SPY decline observed within five sessions, require three rising closes, a reclaim of the 10-session mean, and improving 50-session sector breadth; otherwise SHY.
